chunks: From him, from Ibn Mahbub, from Khalid ibn Nafi', from Hamzah ibn Humran, who said:

I asked Aba Abdillah عليه السلام about a thief who assaulted a Muslim man, wounded him, and usurped his property. Then afterward the thief repented, looked for property equivalent to what he had usurped from the man, and carried it to him, intending to give it back to him and seek absolution from him for what he had done to him; but he found that the man had died. So he asked those who knew him: had he left an heir? And he asked me to ask you about that so that the matter may end at your statement.

He said: Abu Abdillah عليه السلام said: “If the deceased man had entered into clientage with a man from among the Muslims, and he had undertaken his liability and his affairs, and he had made that binding upon himself with witnesses, then the inheritance of the deceased belongs to him. But if the deceased had not entered into clientage with anyone until he died, then his inheritance belongs to the Imam of the Muslims.”

So I said to him: what is the condition of the usurper in what is between him and Allah, Exalted is He? He said: “If he delivers the property to the Imam of the Muslims, then he is safe. But as for the wound, retribution for wounds will be taken from him on the Day of Judgment.”

key_terms.إِمَامِ ٱلْمُسْلِمِينَ: the Imam who holds authority over the affairs of the Muslims
key_terms.سَارِقٍ: a thief who unlawfully took property
key_terms.مِيرَاثَ: inheritance or estate left by the deceased
key_terms.وَارِثًا: an heir entitled to inherit from the deceased
key_terms.يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Judgment when final retribution is taken
key_terms.ٱلْجِرَاحَةُ: the bodily wound or injury inflicted

ai.seo_question: What should a repentant thief do if the person whose property he stole has died without a known heir?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling concerning stolen property when the victim has died and no ordinary heir is known. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام explains that such wealth goes either to one who had lawfully assumed the deceased’s allegiance and liability, or otherwise to the Imam of the Muslims, while bodily injury remains a matter of qisas on the Day of Judgment.
